questions.q: In "Know what home healthcare is Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Name the team: the person, family, support worker, nurse, doctor and therapists.
Ask clients for feedback after the first month.
Check the home for falls risks: loose mats, clutter, poor light, wet floors, stairs.
Explain each step before you start and ask if the person is ready.

questions.q: In "Know the rules, training and scope in Canada Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Explain that personal support worker training and registries differ by province; check the current requirements locally.
Store medicines safely as the plan says.
Where allowed, remind or assist with medicines as the plan says; check the current rule for your role and province.
Report changes quickly to the nurse or supervisor.

questions.q: In "Keep the person and yourself safe Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Explain each step before you start and ask if the person is ready.
Speak simply and use the person's language where you can; use an interpreter when needed.
Wash hands and use gloves as the infection control training says.
Know the signs that a medicine mistake needs urgent help and call at once.

questions.q: In "Provide personal care with dignity Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write notes the same day: what you did, what you saw, what the person said.
Keep logs of visits, incidents and feedback; review them monthly.
Explain each step before you start and ask if the person is ready.
Plan visits by area and time windows; keep a buffer for delays.

questions.q: In "Support medicines and health tasks within scope Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Price visits: hourly rate = (target income + costs) / hours you can really work; ask a licensed accountant about tax and insurance.
Where allowed, remind or assist with medicines as the plan says; check the current rule for your role and province.
Speak simply and use the person's language where you can; use an interpreter when needed.
Check that smoke alarms work and that exits are clear, and report any fault to the family or supervisor.

questions.q: In "Observe, record and communicate Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Explain the difference between a care plan and a service agreement.
Plan travel time between visits and add it to your working hours.
Write notes the same day: what you did, what you saw, what the person said.
Check the name on the medicine label against the plan before any reminder.

questions.q: In "Work with families, culture and other services Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Check the name on the medicine label against the plan before any reminder.
Report changes quickly to the nurse or supervisor.
Write 'reported to' with a name and time for every change you report.
Share only what the person agrees to share with the family.

questions.q: In "Run a home care service for real Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Ask clients for feedback after the first month.
Know local services: meal programmes, adult day programmes, respite and equipment loans.
Wash hands and use gloves as the infection control training says.
